macro.regime: AI-led risk-on rally extends to fresh records against a hawkish-paused (not pivoted) Fed, with credit stress tentatively stabilizing rather than resolving
macro.narrative: Monday's US cash session extended the AI-led rally to fresh records: the S&P 500 rose 0.66% to 7,773.95, the Nasdaq Composite closed at a record 27,477.31 (+1.05%) on broad mega-cap AI strength (SpaceX +7%, Nvidia and Tesla +2%, Meta and Microsoft both higher), the Dow added 0.18%, and the VIX ticked up marginally to 15.52 (+1.37%) off Friday's 15.31 -- still a complacent level. Fed pricing firmed further hawkish rather than pivoting: Oct 28 hold odds held near 82-83% (Kalshi/CME) while December hike odds actually firmed to roughly 68-84% across venues (up from ~65-77% last week), with the Committee's internal split on display this week via dovish Bowman and hawkish Schmid speeches today/tomorrow ahead of Wednesday/Thursday's FOMC minutes, and the 10-year yield holding just off its ~5.32% intraweek 24-year high (easing to roughly 5.26-5.28% Monday). The one genuinely new wrinkle since Monday is credit: broad HY OAS, which widened sharply from 2.93% to a 3.24% peak on Oct 1, has since eased back toward roughly 3.10% -- a tentative stabilization rather than a reversal, with CCC-and-below OAS still pinned near a cycle-high ~1,215bps. Energy diverged Monday (USO -2.29% even as XLE +1.00%), as a reported Saudi price cut for Asia-bound crude and Kpler data showing Hormuz flows back above pre-war levels offset continuing Houthi strikes on Aramco facilities and Saudi's newly full-scale offensive to retake Houthi-held Yemen. Net: regime intact and marginally more constructive than Monday on the credit stabilization and record equity closes, offset by firmer December hike odds.
